Controlled single-seed experiments show that greater information per player improves estimation accuracy and narrows uncertainty intervals, although distinguishing small differences remains difficult and confident conclusions about near-null effects can become more frequent. Applications involving Giroud--Vardy and Berardi--Sansone similarly yield estimated differences that are small relative to their posterior uncertainty. These findings highlight an important distinction between predicting the outcome of a shot and establishing whether one player would be more likely to convert it. The proposed framework makes this distinction explicit by evaluating alternative shooters on fixed recorded opportunities while accounting for their contextual exposure. The resulting comparisons concern conditional conversion rather than the causal consequences of replacing a player in a match.

Signal Processing.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
Signal Processing.summary: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. Transistor-level SKY130 simulations show that the second run gives the gradient within 1.9%; that hardware linearisation permits large, noise-robust error signals; that a 13-cell network learns the Iris data set; and that learning in situ restores mismatched circuits on which software-trained weights fail, from 53-63% to 88-96% test accuracy.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 5 figures, Submitted to ISCAS 2027

Signal Processing.title: Hybrid Monostatic and Bistatic Sensing for Target Localization in OFDM Systems under Phase Noise
Signal Processing.summary: In hybrid monostatic-bistatic orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) sensing, each sensing node receives a superposition of monostatic and bistatic target returns, whose phase-noise (PN) characteristics differ fundamentally due to oscillator sharing. While monostatic sensing benefits from partial PN cancellation through the common transmit-receive oscillator, bistatic sensing involves independent oscillators and is therefore more strongly affected by PN. In this paper, we characterize the joint residual differential PN statistics of these superimposed components in a centralized two-node sensing system and quantify their impact on target localization via theoretical lower bounds considering three different receivers: (i) PN-free ideal receiver, (ii) PN-aware receiver that exploits the joint PN statistics, and (iii) PN-ignorant receiver that neglects PN.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshop on Positioning and Sensing Over Wireless Networks

Signal Processing.title: Toward Motion Capture Textiles: A Batteryless IMU Array Powered and Networked Through a Conductive-Fabric Bus
Signal Processing.summary: Motion capture is increasingly important in healthcare, rehabilitation, and sports applications. However, conventional vision-based systems require camera infrastructure and line-of-sight conditions, limiting their use in daily environments. This paper proposes a location-independent platform for motion capture, based on an array of IMU (inertial measurement unit) sensor nodes without individual wiring or onboard batteries, enabled by two-dimensional communication and power delivery over conductive fabric. Pipeline processing in each sensor node, combined with a token-passing protocol, enables collision-free and stable data acquisition at 50 Hz. Real-time three-dimensional reconstruction of flexible objects is further demonstrated by applying Hermite spline interpolation to orientation data from grid-aligned IMUs. Against a cylinder of known radius, the reconstructed surface deviates by 2.60 mm RMS over the 225 mm span of the array. The reconstruction is formulated for the quasi-static regime, and this letter empirically validates it in that regime. The hardware platform and communication protocol implemented in this work enable further investigation toward dynamic motion capture textiles.
Signal Processing.comment: 4 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in IEEE Sensors Letters

Signal Processing.title: Bilinear Compressive Security with Finitely Many Samples
Signal Processing.summary:
Bilinear Compressive Security (BCS) is a lightweight encryption scheme that combines compressed sensing with a fresh random convolution filter to improve resistance against key-recovery attacks under key reuse. Previous work derived information-theoretic guarantees for BCS by relating key identifiability to phase retrieval under the assumption that an adversary has access to the full ciphertext distribution induced by the random filter. In practice, however, an adversary only observes finitely many encryptions, leaving the security of BCS in the finite-sample regime largely unexplored.
  In this paper, we study key recovery from only finitely many observations. We first develop a covariance-based attack that estimates the linear measurements from repeated encryptions of the same plaintext and subsequently recovers the secret measurement matrix. We analyze the estimation procedure and derive finite-sample guarantees together with corresponding sample-complexity bounds. We further investigate the complete attack experimentally and compare its observed recovery behavior with the previously established information-theoretic identifiability results.
  Our experiments show two qualitatively different recovery regimes on the structure of the measurement matrix. For dense matrices, including Gaussian matrices, the number of measurements required for successful recovery appears to grow linearly with the signal dimension. This differs from the worst-case behavior suggested by information theory. In contrast, for matrices with sparse rows, we observe a quadratic growth consistent with the theoretical bound.
  These results suggest that the sparsity structure of the measurement matrix plays an important role in the security of BCS and should be taken into account when selecting parameters and designing practical instances of the scheme.

Signal Processing.title: DeepPV-MRF: End-to-End Partial-Volume Fraction Estimation from MR Fingerprinting Time Series
Signal Processing.summary:
Background: Estimating subvoxel tissue fractions from magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is challenging. Conventional dictionary matching and segmentation pipelines can propagate errors from intermediate parametric maps into tissue fraction estimates.
  Purpose: We introduce DeepPV-MRF, a deep learning framework that directly estimates voxel-wise tissue fractions from raw MRF signals.
  Methods: A cascaded spatial-temporal network was trained on subject-derived Bloch simulations with radial k-space undersampling. The network combines temporal encoding and spatial U-Net refinement to estimate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), gray matter (GM), and white matter (WM) fractions without intermediate T1/T2 maps. We compared DeepPV-MRF with partial-volume dictionary matching (PV-DM) and pseudoinverse estimation (PV-Pinv) using simulated and in vivo data.
  Results: DeepPV-MRF outperformed both methods across acquisition settings. In single-shot simulations, CSF/WM/GM mean absolute errors were 0.0418/0.0744/0.0757, versus 0.1281/0.2443/0.2958 for PV-DM and 0.2021/0.2793/0.2630 for PV-Pinv. Corresponding structural similarity values were 0.960/0.916/0.922. In vivo results showed sharper anatomical boundaries and smoother tissue transitions, while cross-shot analysis indicated improved consistency across volunteers.
  Conclusions: DeepPV-MRF enables accurate and efficient direct tissue fraction estimation from MRF signals, particularly with limited shots. Further validation is needed before clinical deployment.

Signal Processing.title: Comparative Analysis and Behavioral Modelling of Power Amplifiers in FR3
Signal Processing.summary: Power amplifier (PA) nonlinearity is a critical transmitter impairment in the upper mid-band (7 GHz to 24 GHz), designated as Frequency Range 3 (FR3) in emerging 6G standardisation. The 3GPP PA model baseline, TR 38.803 Annex A, was derived from 2.1 GHz and 28 GHz measurements and has not been revisited yet for FR3 standards work. This paper addresses that gap with characterisation measurements of multiple PA devices-under-test (DUTs), driven into gain compression in the 7 GHz and 15 GHz bands with 100 MHz and 200 MHz bandwidth. Memoryless polynomial and Generalized Memory Polynomial (GMP) behavioral models are extracted by least-squares regression and compared with 3GPP models spanning FR1 and FR2. The GaN PA DUT is modelled best at a higher nonlinear order and shows markedly stronger phase distortion than the wideband PA. The memory terms of the GMP model measurably improve the Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) at all operating points. An orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) ambiguity function analysis from the Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) literature, using the extracted models, illustrates how PA compression raises the sidelobe floor of the sensing response. These results provide a reference for PA impairment modelling in FR3, directly applicable to ISAC system design. All model coefficients and measurement data are publicly available [1].
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at 2026 IEEE 1st Annual Integrated Sensing and Communication Conference (ISAC)

Signal Processing.title: CORTEG: Foundation Models Enable Cross-Modality Representation Transfer from Scalp to Intracranial Brain Recordings
Signal Processing.summary: Intracranial electrocorticography (ECoG) offers high signal-to-noise access to cortical activity for brain-computer interfaces, yet limited per-patient data has led most prior work to rely on small, subject-specific decoders that neglect information shared across patients. We investigate whether large pretrained scalp-EEG foundation models (EEG FMs) can be adapted to ECoG, enabling cross-patient learning and competitive decoding performance while calibrating to a held-out patient in 10-30 minutes on a single GPU. We introduce CORTEG, a cross-modality transfer framework that combines a pretrained EEG FM backbone, an electrode-aware KNNSoftFourier spatial adapter, a dual-stream tokenizer for low-frequency and high-gamma activity, and a leave-one-subject-out fine-tuning strategy. We evaluate CORTEG on two challenging regression tasks: public finger-trajectory regression ($n=9$) and private audio-envelope regression ($n=16$). CORTEG achieves state-of-the-art mean performance on both tasks, achieving the highest mean correlation among the compared methods on the public finger benchmark and larger, statistically significant gains on the audio task and in low-data-per-patient calibration. We further validate CORTEG on the public BrainTreebank stereo-EEG classification tasks, where it also performs strongly. Furthermore, CORTEG outperforms the compared intracranial-EEG foundation models across the continuous regression tasks. Feature analyses align with neurophysiology, and latent representations capture low-dimensional finger-movement structure. Together, these results provide systematic evidence that scalp-EEG pretraining can be repurposed across intracranial recording modalities and tasks, enabling data-efficient neural decoders that can adapt to new patients.
Signal Processing.comment: Camera-ready version with new BrainTree Bank experiments and comparisons with iEEG FMs

Signal Processing.title: Simultaneous Secure Communications and Sensing Privacy with Full Duplex MIMO Radios
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes a Full Duplex (FD) framework for safeguarding Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) against a passive multi-antenna Eavesdropper (Eve). The adversary is modeled as both a communication and sensing threat, seeking to decode uplink data streams and estimate the surrounding scene. Eve's threat is quantified through two worst-case requirements over a location uncertainty region: a minimum secrecy rate for data confidentiality and a minimum eavesdropping Cramer-Rao Bound (CRB) for sensing privacy. We derive the eavesdropping information measures governing both data interception and scene inference, showcasing that transmitting Artificial Noise (AN) can degrade Eve's capabilities through the inverse interference-plus-noise covariance. Exploiting the underlying structure of the problem, we characterize finite-power local and robust feasibility conditions for target secrecy-privacy pairs. The analysis showcases that AN is fundamentally subspace-limited: increasing power is beneficial only along Eve's communication channel and sensing-derivative directions illuminated by the effective AN subspace. Finally, we formulate an AN power allocation problem that is solved via monotone branch-and-bound, and numerical evaluations quantify the AN power required to guarantee joint secrecy and sensing privacy.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures

Signal Processing.title: Resilient Angle-Constrained Formation Control and Localization Under DoS Attacks (Extended Version)
Signal Processing.summary: This paper studies resilient angle-constrained leader--follower formation control and localization of multi-agent systems under asynchronous denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, which block individual sensing and communication links. To preserve the well-posedness of angle-based localization, an all-or-nothing triangle integrity protocol (ANTIP) is proposed to convert edge-wise attacks into triangle-wise ones, and DoS attacks are classified into localizability-maintained and localizability-broken attacks. First, with relative position measurements over attack-free links, resilient formation tracking laws are designed for leaders with constant velocities and with time-varying velocities comprising translational, rotational, and scaling motions. These laws guarantee asymptotic tracking and finite-time recovery of tracking, respectively, when the duration of localizability-broken attacks is suitably bounded. Second, with only angle measurements and communications, a resilient simultaneous localization and formation control (RSLAF) scheme is developed. It combines a finite-time distributed observer, which estimates the exosystem matrices and states under asynchronous DoS attacks, with a perturbation-based localization law that prevents localization from getting stuck at degenerate configurations. The theoretical results are rigorously proved and illustrated by numerical simulations.

Signal Processing.title: The Derivation of The Probability of Error for BPSK, 16-QAM and 64-QAM in Rayleigh Fading Channel: A Unified Approach
Signal Processing.summary: Understanding the probability of error is paramount in the design and analysis of digital communication systems, particularly in Rayleigh fading channels where signal impairments are prevalent. This article presents a unified approach for deriving the probability of error formulations applicable to Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK), 16-Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (16-QAM), and 64-QAM in Rayleigh fading channels. This article presents a general approach to derive the probability of error formulations applicable to Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK), 16-Quadruple Amplitude Modulation (16-QAM) and 64-QAM in Rayleigh fading channels. The derivation process encompasses the unique characteristics of each modulation scheme and the statistical properties of Rayleigh fading providing a comprehensive framework to analyze error performance. By establishing a unified formulation, this approach simplifies the analysis and facilitates a deeper understanding of error probability behavior across different modulation schemes. The derived formulations offer insights into the impact of fading-induced impairments on system performance, allowing for accurate prediction and optimization of communication systems in real-world fading environments. The insights and techniques presented herein serve as a valuable resource for researchers, engineers, and practitioners engaged in the design and optimization of communication systems operating in challenging fading environments.

Signal Processing.title: A Knowledge-Centric Communication For Autonomous Cislunar Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Future lunar infrastructure requires communication as a persistent service rather than a mission specific capability. Communication, digital twin, and artificial intelligence (AI) research have advanced autonomy independently while largely assuming that system state can eventually be reconciled with ground truth. Cislunar communication violates this assumption because propagation delay is fundamentally limited by the speed of light, visibility is governed by orbital geometry, and autonomous decisions often precede confirming observations. Here we introduce a knowledge-centric communication framework in which a digital twin continuously integrates delayed observations, communication physics, learned models, uncertainty quantification, and mission objectives into an evolving Operational Knowledge State. To quantify what is known, how uncertain it remains, and how current it is, we define two quantities over the fused Bayesian belief maintained for each communication link: \emph{Knowledge Entropy}, the differential entropy of the posterior belief, and \emph{Knowledge Freshness}, which generalizes Age of Information (AoI) from a single information stream to the temporal validity of the fused Operational Knowledge State. We prove that distributed knowledge fusion systematically improves operational knowledge by reducing uncertainty and demonstrate its importance for mission success through simulations and comparisons with flight data from the Longjiang-2 lunar micro-satellite.
Signal Processing.comment: 22 pages, 8 Figures, 2 Tables

Signal Processing.title: A Wireless World Model for AI-Native 6G Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Integrating AI into the physical layer is a cornerstone of 6G networks. However, current data-driven approaches struggle to generalize across dynamic environments because they lack an intrinsic understanding of electromagnetic wave propagation. We introduce the Wireless World Model (WWM), a multi-modal foundation framework predicting the spatiotemporal evolution of wireless channels by internalizing the causal relationship between 3D geometry and signal dynamics. Pre-trained on a massive ray-traced multi-modal dataset, WWM overcomes the data authenticity gap, further validated under real-world measurement data. Using a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a multi-modal mixture-of-experts Transformer, WWM fuses channel state information, 3D point clouds, and user trajectories into a unified representation. Across the five key downstream tasks supported by WWM, it achieves remarkable performance in seen environments, unseen generalization scenarios, and real-world measurements, consistently outperforming SOTA uni-modal foundation models and task-specific models. This paves the way for physics-aware 6G intelligence that adapts to the physical world.

Signal Processing.title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition
Signal Processing.summary: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. We evaluate the proposed dataset across three tasks: self-supervised representation learning, vessel-type classification, and MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Experiments on DeepShip and ShipsEar demonstrate the effectiveness of ONCship for acoustic representation learning, with joint pre-training on ONCship and AudioSet achieving a classification accuracy of 62.45% on DeepShip through linear probing. Furthermore, incorporating ONCship as auxiliary training data improves downstream vessel-type classification performance. Beyond conventional vessel-type classification, we further investigate MMSI-Level Vessel Classification, treating each vessel as a distinct identity. Experimental results show that models fine-tuned with different loss functions achieve Top-1 accuracies exceeding 53% and Top-5 accuracies approaching 69%, demonstrating the feasibility of distinguishing individual vessels through MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Overall, ONCship provides a valuable resource for underwater acoustic representation learning and vessel recognition, while its rich vessel-level metadata enables further exploration of MMSI-Level Vessel Classification.

Signal Processing.title: Low-complexity Soft-decision LLR Calculations for Next-generation IM-DD Systems with RIN
Signal Processing.summary: The demand for higher speeds in intra-data center interconnects will eventually require high-order pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) combined with soft-decision (SD) forward error correction (FEC). The laser relative intensity noise (RIN) is an important noise impairment that limits the performance of high-speed intensity-modulation (IM) and direct-detection (DD) systems, as it induces a channel with signal-dependent noise. In this paper, we show that an accurate calculation of the log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) is critical for the performance of the SD-FEC decoder in RIN-dominated IM-DD systems. First, we show that assuming signal-independent additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) statistics to compute LLRs results in a significant penalty in performance. As an alternative, we propose a low-complexity piecewise linear approximation of the exact LLRs of Gray-coded PAM-4 and PAM-8 for the RIN-dominated IM-DD channel. We show using the generalized mutual information that our approximation results in no performance loss versus using exact LLRs, unlike the AWGN-like assumption. Furthermore, we validate the analysis with bit error rate (BER) performance of SD decoding. We show that our approximation matches the BERs achieved using exact LLRs. Therefore, our approximation avoids a BER error floor penalty of up to 7.2 times using an extended Hamming code with PAM-4, and up to 2.41 dB of optical modulation amplitude penalty using high-code-rate low-density parity-check codes with PAM-8 for the same target BER.

Signal Processing.title: Gauge-Invariant, Parameter-Insensitive Regularization for Potential Recovery from Flow on Directed Graphs
Signal Processing.summary: Recovering a latent potential from observed flow on a directed graph (a discrete Poisson problem with Dirichlet boundaries) is ill-posed, and the standard fix backfires: ridge regularization shrinks toward a gauge-meaningless origin, collapsing and reversing the recovered ordering ($+0.81\to-0.42$ rank correlation against a planted ground truth). The gauge-invariant graph Dirichlet energy removes the hazard and delivers parameter-insensitivity: the estimate is stable across four orders of magnitude in $λ$, whereas ridge inverts the ordering for every $λ>0$. We prove the reduced solve is SPD and preserves dynamic range exactly where ridge collapses it, and localize absorbing boundaries from flow alone via a Poisson residual. The $H^1$ seminorm is classical; what is new is the gauge diagnosis, the parameter-insensitivity it buys, and an ablation showing the result is robust to the extraction method. On three public clickstream corpora the gauge-invariant estimate retains $28$--$41\%$ of the interior dynamic range while ridge collapses to as little as $0.2\%$. The same gauge invariance carries into graph neural networks -- neutralizing the constant mode per layer prevents the oversmoothing that collapses a deep directed GCN -- linking this classical inverse problem to a central question in graph learning.
Signal Processing.comment: 19 pages, 6 figures, Proceedings of the Fifth Learning on Graphs Conference (LoG 2026), PMLR 338

Signal Processing.title: Antenna Positioning and Beamforming Optimization in MA Enabled Secure ISAC Systems: A Gradient-Based Meta Learning Approach
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) significantly improves spectral efficiency but introduces security risks regarding the interception of embedded communication signals. This paper proposes an movable antenna (MA)-enabled secure ISAC system that utilizes the spatial degrees of freedom of MA to mitigate these risks. Then, a problem is formulated to maximize the system secrecy rate by jointly optimizing antenna positioning, transmit beamforming, and artificial noise. However, the principal challenge arises from the non-convexity of the optimization problem and the strong coupling of the optimization variables. Generally, traditional optimization methods for this problem suffer from complex mathematical derivations, while existing deep learning approaches rely heavily on the training data distribution. To address these issues, we introduce a gradient-based meta learning (GML) algorithm, which works without pre-training and demonstrates favorable performance. Specifically, the algorithm establishes a neural network for each optimization variable, where the gradient of the objective function with respect to the variable serves as the input, and the output of the network determines the variable's update step. By handling the constraints and constructing penalty terms, the global loss function is used to guide the optimization process. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves satisfactory performance in terms of both communication security and sensing capabilities.

Signal Processing.title: Hardware-friendly Baseband Design and Performance Analysis for LEO Broadband LoS-MIMO Systems
Signal Processing.summary: High-frequency and broadband line-of-sight multiple-input multiple-output (LoS-MIMO) is a key solution for massive space-to-Earth data downlinks. However, in low Earth orbit (LEO) scenarios, it faces spatial rank deficiency from time-frequency coupling correlation and clock deviations from distributed oscillators. This paper establishes a dynamic effective channel throughput (ECT) framework incorporating waterfall characteristics of forward error correction. A hardware-friendly OFDM-based transceiver architecture with subband-adaptive truncation and dynamic timing recovery to achieve robust spatial decoupling is proposed. Through rigorous closed-form derivations, the equivalent signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) under joint errors is quantified, and an optimal scheduling algorithm combining truncation with variable coding and modulation is proposed to maximize ECT. Simulations confirm that the design circumvents outages caused by spatial notches with low complexity, stably enhancing the potential average throughput of a single dual-polarized beam to over 100 Gbps, providing a reliable theoretical foundation and baseband solution for next-generation high-throughput satellites.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures

Signal Processing.title: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Integrated Sensing and Communication in IoT C-RAN
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with cloud radio access networks (C-RAN) unifies two foundational technologies for the Internet of Things (IoT), enabling both high-data-rate transmission and accurate environmental awareness. This paper investigates an uplink C-RAN system where multiple remote radio units (RRUs) jointly serve user equipment devices (UEs) and sense a target. We demonstrate that only a subset of RRUs is typically needed to meet sensing requirements, while energy is potentially conserved by deactivating redundant sensing RRUs. Motivated by this, we aim to improve the system's energy efficiency (EE) by jointly optimizing RRU activation, user association, and power allocation, while ensuring localization accuracy through the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). To address this problem, we propose a model-based iterative algorithm that integrates optimal user association, decision tree-based selection of sensing RRUs, and fixed-point power allocation. This algorithm is further used to train a graph neural network (GNN) framework, ISAC-GNN, to overcome scalability and computational complexity limitations. Our theoretical analysis ensures performance guarantees, while a semi-supervised training strategy enhances stability and generalization. Simulation results demonstrate that ISAC-GNN reduces inference time by 67% relative to the model-based approach, enabling real-time implementation for ISAC system resource management. In addition, ISAC-GNN allows scalable deployment across various system scenarios without retraining the model.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 5 figures, and 7 tables. Published in IEEE IOTJ

Signal Processing.title: Low-Complexity Channel Estimation Framework for Non-Square UPA-Assisted XL-MIMO Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Low-complexity channel state information acquisition is crucial for extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems. However, practical deployments of non-square uniform planar arrays (UPAs) in hybrid-field environments face prohibitive computational complexity and degraded estimation accuracy due to limited elevation angle-of-arrival (AoA) resolution and deteriorated channel sparsity. To tackle these challenges, we propose a low-complexity channel estimation framework. First, an antenna-domain extrapolation scheme synthesizes a virtually enlarged vertical aperture via the spatial correlation among adjacent elements, breaking the elevation resolution limit. The framework then disentangles the parameter coupling by transforming the two-dimensional joint search into two sequential one-dimensional searches. Specifically, elevation AoAs are extracted via an extrapolation-enhanced discrete Fourier transform-Newtonized orthogonal matching pursuit (NOMP) algorithm along the virtually enlarged vertical uniform linear array (ULA), while azimuth AoAs, ranges, and gains are acquired utilizing a discrete fractional Fourier transform-NOMP algorithm along a horizontal ULA. A subspace fitting-driven path matching algorithm pairs these decoupled parameters. To overcome the accuracy bottleneck of the antenna-domain scheme, a correlation-domain extrapolation scheme is further developed by exploiting the structural properties of the spatial correlation matrix to decouple the near-field quadratic and azimuth phase components, yielding a noise-suppressed virtual array. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Signal Processing.title: Train to Stitch: Topology-Preserving Regularization for Interoperable Representations
Signal Processing.summary: As large, powerful pre-trained models become more prevalent, there is growing interest in developing methods that allow different neural networks to be seamlessly combined with little or no direct communication between them. Take autoencoder-based data compression as an example: the ability to independently choose architectures and train encoder and decoder models, while still ensuring they work together, could fundamentally transform how such models are built, deployed, and updated. In this work, we introduce a novel approach that leverages topological regularization to align the latent spaces of two independently trained autoencoder models, entirely eliminating the need for coordination during training. We provide a conditional theoretical analysis showing how the structural agreement encouraged by our regularizer can translate into approximate geometric compatibility between independently learned representations. Reconstruction experiments validate this approach empirically, substantially narrowing the interoperability gap across multiple datasets.

Signal Processing.title: Probe Sets for Nonlinear Kalman Filtering: Multi-Center Gains and Covariance Recalibration
Signal Processing.summary: Kalman filters (KFs) choose the gain as the product of the state-measurement cross-covariance and the inverse of the innovation covariance. In nonlinear systems, the predictive distribution generally changes shape, and these covariances require approximation. Conventional nonlinear KFs approximate them around a single center, the predicted state. They can produce inaccurate gains and overconfident covariance estimates when one local approximation does not represent the measurement geometry across the uncertainty region. To address this issue, we introduce probe sets, small covariance-scaled collections of states at which the filter repeats its local approximation. We then select the gain that minimizes the average covariance reported by these local approximations. The same construction is used in our previously proposed covariance recalibration step to improve covariance consistency. The construction applies to different KF variants without requiring a specific approximation rule. For quadratic measurements, we derive conditions under which probing yields lower normalized true error variance than the corresponding single-center gain when prediction uncertainty is sufficiently understated. We apply the framework to four KF variants and compare the resulting filters with multiple baselines across 300 randomized setups for each of two systems. The results show that probing preserves typical accuracy while substantially reducing covariance inconsistency and the rare large-error trajectories that dominate the root mean square of per-run errors. The code is available at https://github.com/Shida-Jiang/Probe_KF.

Systems and Control.title: Adaptive Dead-Zone Dual Sliding Mode Observer for Reliable Electrochemical Model-Based SOC Estimation
Systems and Control.summary: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for safe and efficient lithium-ion battery operation. Electrochemical models provide physically grounded SOC estimates, but nonlinear voltage dynamics and coupled state-parameter errors can destabilize online adaptation. This paper proposes an adaptive dead-zone dual sliding-mode observer (ADZ-DSMO) based on an improved extended single-particle (IESP) model. A state SMO estimates SOC-related states, while a parameter SMO updates dominant model parameters. An online-computable, Lyapunov-guided adaptive boundary selectively gates parameter updates while the state observer remains active at every sampling step. Validation on a Panasonic NCR18650PF cell under 1C and 3C constant-current discharge and the Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule (UDDS) and New European Driving Cycle (NEDC) profiles shows lower SOC estimation errors than conventional dual SMO and the IESP-based dual extended Kalman filter (DEKF). Compared with DEKF, the proposed observer provides faster recovery from a 30% initial SOC bias. Selective parameter updating reduces the average per-step computation time compared with the always-updating dual SMO. Temperature tests and capacity-based, model-generated aging cases further assess robustness. These results support adaptive gating as a means of reducing error propagation and computational overhead in electrochemical-model-based joint state-parameter estimation.
Systems and Control.comment: 45 pages, 8 figures, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306261926016995

Systems and Control.title: Integer-Free Control Synthesis for Signal Temporal Logic via Ranked Implicants
Systems and Control.summary: This paper proposes an integer-free method for control synthesis of nonlinear discrete-time systems under finite-horizon Signal Temporal Logic (STL) constraints. Instead of introducing integer variables, we consider the discrete choices of the specification in a ranked order and solve a standard nonlinear program for each selected choice until a satisfying trajectory is found. We first define implicants as sets of timed atomic constraints whose joint satisfaction is sufficient to satisfy the specification. A reference trajectory obtained from a smooth approximation of the STL robustness is used to rank these implicants. Fixing one implicant turns the problem into a standard nonlinear program with no auxiliary weights or bilinear terms. If the solution does not satisfy the specification, the next implicant will be considered. We prove soundness and completeness of our method relative to the nonlinear programming solver. Numerical evaluation on nonlinear multi-agent systems shows that our proposed method identifies satisfying trajectories where the exact continuous reformulation fails, and moreover, it is faster than a mixed-integer formulation of the same specification.
Systems and Control.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures

Systems and Control.title: Adaptive Prescribed Performance Trajectory Tracking for Uncertain Autonomous Underwater Vehicles With Input Saturation
Systems and Control.summary: Accurate trajectory tracking is essential for autonomous underwater vehicles operating with uncertain hydrodynamics and limited thruster authority. This paper develops a low-complexity adaptive prescribed performance controller for uncertain underwater vehicle dynamics with coupled and saturated inputs. The proposed method adapts the performance functions directly through the mismatch between the requested and saturated control inputs, enlarging the performance funnels only when the available actuation cannot meet the nominal specifications. A coupled invariant-set analysis establishes boundedness of all closed-loop signals, prescribed bounds on the filtered tracking errors, and explicit feasibility conditions. Comparative simulations on a BlueROV2 underwater vehicle show that the adaptive design maintains prescribed performance during a figure-eight maneuver, whereas conventional prescribed performance control loses feasibility under input limits. A real-time pool experiment further demonstrates stable trajectory tracking and the practical implementation of the proposed method on an underwater robotic platform.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Supplementary video included as ancillary material

Systems and Control.title: Congestion Price Uncertainty From Interconnection Queue by Monte Carlo Sampling
Systems and Control.summary: The generation interconnection queue adds discrete uncertainty to power grid congestion price estimates on the project planning timescale. The conventional approach to this uncertainty is to make an informed guess of the single or few most likely configurations of generators that interconnect. In this paper, we show that Monte Carlo sampling is a more effective alternative. Given an estimate of the joint probability distribution of generator interconnections, a small number of samples yields good estimates of the congestion distribution. Crucially, this problem is not about rare events, but rather about the expected congestion over the worst times of the year, which makes congestion a common outcome over the distribution of interconnection events. We give empirical results on a 2000-bus network, averaging price outcomes from security-constrained DCOPF over eight different loading scenarios. For each line and contingency of the network, we estimate the full distribution as well as mean price and probability of exceeding a price threshold. Single-point estimates are unreliable and can be misleading about whether a line is likely to be congested. Combining the top k probability configurations yields improved estimates; however, sampling the same number from a distribution gives a more robust result of similar accuracy, as well as error estimates. Including correlation in the distribution model introduces small changes, showing that standard Bernoulli distributions suffice in most cases. The sampling approach is also applicable to large-load interconnection and should be of interest for planning both generation and large-load projects.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 9 figures

Systems and Control.title: Objective-Aware Policy Orchestration for O-RAN Service Provisioning
Systems and Control.summary: O-RAN enables the deployment of heterogeneous control and provisioning algorithms through open interfaces and programmable intelligent controllers. However, most existing intelligent O-RAN solutions rely on a single optimization strategy designed for a fixed operational objective, limiting their ability to adapt when network conditions or operator priorities change. This paper proposes an objective-aware policy orchestration framework that selects the most appropriate provisioning policy for each control window based on the current network context and operator objective. The framework orchestrates a portfolio of heterogeneous provisioning experts using contextual-bandit learning. Two policy selectors, Linear Thompson Sampling and a Bootstrap Tree ensemble, are evaluated against static provisioning policies and a deterministic rule-based orchestrator. Experimental results show that learning-based policy orchestration can effectively adapt policy selection to varying operating conditions, improving overall objective-aware performance while preserving the modularity of existing provisioning algorithms.

Systems and Control.title: From Global to Local: Hierarchical Probabilistic Verification for Reachability Learning
Systems and Control.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides formal safety guarantees for nonlinear systems. However, it becomes computationally intractable in high-dimensional settings, motivating learning-based approximations that may introduce unsafe errors or overly optimistic safe sets. In this work, we propose a hierarchical probabilistic verification framework for reachability learning that bridges offline global certification and online local refinement. We first construct a coarse, conservative under-approximation of the reach-avoid safe set using scenario optimization, providing an efficient global probabilistic certificate. We then introduce an online local refinement module that is structurally anchored to the global certificate and recovers regions excluded by the global verification. This refinement reduces conservatism while focusing computation on critical regions of the state space. Integrated with a condition-based switching mechanism between a learned reachability policy and a model-based controller, the proposed framework improves success rates in goal-reaching tasks with safety constraints, as demonstrated in drone-racing simulation experiments.
Systems and Control.comment: This paper has been accepted by the IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS) and jointly by the IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC), 2026

Systems and Control.title: Planning to Learn: Real-Time Robust Adaptive Control on the GPU with Guaranteed Future Learning
Systems and Control.summary: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. Across nonlinear robotic systems, A-SLS reduces reachable-tube conservativeness, maintains real-time performance, and scales to whole-body control for a quadruped with 61 states, 8 uncertain parameters, and 12 control inputs. We further demonstrate the approach on hardware, where a physical Crazyflie drone learns an uncertain dynamics parameter online to stabilize on the fly.

Systems and Control.title: Co-designing a Layered Control Architecture
Systems and Control.summary: Layered control architectures (LCAs) are ubiquitous in complex engineering systems. However, in practice they are largely designed ad hoc and mostly dictated by the experience of the designer. This is because there is currently no systematic and practically applicable theory available to holistically design LCAs. Hence, systematically reasoning about the optimality, stability, and feasibility of the LCA design is not possible. We set a first step toward such a theory by presenting a framework for co-designing a two-layer LCA for a linear time-invariant plant. The resulting co-design problem optimizes over architectural design variables (e.g., reduced order model dimension and sampling ratio between the layers) and tuning-based design variables (e.g., the numerical values of the feedback gain or the matrices of the reduced order model), all subject to constraints that ensure stability, feasibility, and compute properties of the closed-loop LCA. The proposed formulation allows to make informed tradeoffs along the Pareto front traced over different axes of optimality, e.g., speed, accuracy or computational effort. We demonstrate the effect of making various tradeoffs in a simple numerical example.
Systems and Control.comment: 19 pages, extended version

Systems and Control.title: Optimally Trading Energy for Information through Speed Trajectory Optimization of Sustainably Powered Mobile Robots
Systems and Control.summary: Sustainably powered mobile robots enable long-duration observational missions by harvesting energy from the environment. However, effective autonomy requires the robots to make decisions as to how to allocate this energy to maximize information quality over time. In this paper, we study a persistent (infinite-horizon) speed trajectory optimization problem that is posed as a periodic optimal control problem in which a robot repeatedly traverses a fixed closed path, coupling a super-linear propulsion cost with dynamic information gain and decay. Using the information-theoretic quantity of clarity as an information metric, we first derive the necessary conditions for optimal control. We then derive a number of specialized follow-on properties, which characterize (i) the nature of the optimal control when points on the path are of varying importance and when they are of equal importance, along with (ii) a high-speed information limit that is approached when energy reserves approach infinity. We illustrate the information-optimal speed trajectories on a simple example in order to showcase key trends that are followed under the optimized speed profile. This is followed by a simulation study based on the persistent characterization of salinity in the Chesapeake Bay, illustrating the practical merit of applying the results from this work.

Systems and Control.title: Clarity-Driven Adaptive Mission Planning for a Solar-Powered Autonomous Surface Vessel
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive methodology, backed by simulation and experimental results, for an adaptive mission planning strategy that is mathematically grounded in the maximization of the information-driven quantity of clarity. In particular, the methodology introduced in this work addresses the use of sustainably powered autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to perform scientific missions that prioritize locations of maximum interest. Because these locations of maximum interest are not known a priori but are rather identified based on in-situ measurements, online adaptation is essential for mission planning. Furthermore, the reliance on a limited-power renewable resource requires an adaptation strategy that maximizes information gathering subject to mobility restrictions imposed by the renewable resource. Our approach addresses these challenges through a clarity-driven ergodic search, where clarity represents a mathematical quantity that has been rigorously linked to differential (information) entropy. In our approach, a target clarity map is adapted online to reflect the prioritization of certain areas based on in-situ measurements, and an ergodic path planner continually re-plans based on the target clarity map and ASV speed limitations (driven by the renewable propulsion source). Focusing on a solar-powered ASV, we present simulations and experiments conducted at Jordan Lake, North Carolina, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Systems and Control.title: A Response to the Reply Presented in "A Fair Comparison of Sliding-Mode and Immersion-and-Invariance Observers"
Systems and Control.summary: In response to the reply presented in [Muñoz-Vázquez and Sánchez-Torres(2026)], this technical report extends the experimental evaluation of position-feedback velocity observers and adaptive tracking controllers for a pendular system with nonlinear friction reported in [Cervantes-Pérez et al.(2026)]. The immersion and invariance (I&I) adaptive control scheme proposed in [Romero et al.(2025)], whose gains are tuned according to the guidelines presented in [Ortega et al.(2025)], is compared with a control scheme employing the adaptive modi?ed super-twisting observer of [Dávila et al.(2006)], whose observer gains are selected according to the guidelines proposed in [Muñoz-Vázquez and Sánchez-Torres(2026)]. Although these "tuning guidelines" attenuate chattering in certain scenarios, the experimental results reported here show that they do not eliminate it in general.

Systems and Control.title: Navigation by Skylight Polarization via Rayleigh Model Optimization on a Road Vehicle
Systems and Control.summary: Reliable absolute heading estimation is critical for road-vehicle navigation, particularly when magnetic, inertial, or GNSS-based references are degraded. This paper presents a skylight polarization navigation method that estimates vehicle heading by globally optimizing a Rayleigh sky model against measurements from a division-of-focal-plane polarimetric camera. The proposed framework combines a pinhole camera model, a single-scattering Rayleigh polarization model, and a solar position algorithm to synthesize the expected full image angle of polarization distribution for candidate vehicle states. A degree of polarization weighted root mean square error objective function compares measured and simulated polarization patterns, allowing the estimator to use all available sky information while attenuating low confidence pixels caused by clouds, buildings, foliage, and other depolarizing occlusions. Experimental evaluation is performed using three urban road vehicle trajectories collected with a roof mounted polarimetric camera and a high precision dual-antenna GNSS/INS reference system. Results show sub-degree RMS yaw error across all trajectories, ranging from $0.718^{\circ}$ to $0.889^{\circ}$. Compared with representative feature-based and model-based polarization navigation methods, the proposed approach reduces RMS heading error by up to 87% and demonstrates improved robustness to partial sky occlusion.

Systems and Control.title: Electrical Power Grid Reliability Assessment Exposed to Straight Line Winds
Systems and Control.summary: Maintaining the resilience and reliability of electrical power grids under weather driven disturbances is a critical challenge for modern power system planning and operation. Among weather driven hazards, tornadoes and hurricanes are mostly considered for research purpose overlooking straight line winds despite its significant contribution to transmission line outages and cascading effects. Accurate modeling of these events is essential for operational decision making, and long term infrastructure planning and investment. This research explores the probabilistic risk assessment of transmission lines under straight line winds and their impacts on system level performance. The approach examines the probability of transmission towers failure, transmission lines outages, cascading effects, and identify critical transmission lines. The IEEE 118 bus system was utilized to validate the proposed approach and to demonstrate how wind induced component failures propagate throughout the network, affecting power grid reliability.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted at the 2026 North American Power Symposium (NAPS)

Systems and Control.title: Optimal Demand Response-Based Energy Management for Campus Buildings with Battery Energy Storage Systems: A Case Study of the ELB Building
Systems and Control.summary: Buildings account for a significant portion of global electricity consumption, making demand response (DR) an effective strategy for reducing energy costs and improving grid flexibility. This paper presents an optimal energy management framework for a campus building that integrates demand response and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to minimize electricity costs while satisfying operational constraints and occupant comfort requirements. The proposed optimization model schedules building loads and battery charging/discharging based on time-varying electricity prices and building demand profiles. The framework is validated using the Engineering Laboratory Building (ELB) at the University of Michigan-Dearborn as a real-world case study. Four operating scenarios are investigated: (i) baseline operation, (ii) demand response without battery energy storage, (iii) battery energy storage, and (iv) demand response with battery energy storage. Simulation results demonstrate that demand alone reduces the building's electricity cost by approximately 12% compared with conventional operation. When battery energy storage is incorporated, the total electricity cost reduction increases to approximately 26%, highlighting the significant economic benefits of coordinated demand response and energy storage scheduling. The results demonstrate that integrating battery energy storage with demand response substantially enhances the operational flexibility of campus buildings and provides an effective solution for cost-effective and sustainable building energy management.

Systems and Control.title: Optimization via a Control-Centric Framework
Systems and Control.summary: Optimization plays a central role in intelligent systems and cyber-physical technologies, where speed and reliability of convergence directly impact performance. In control theory, optimization is the foundation of widely-used design methodologies such as linear quadratic regulation, $H_\infty$ control, and model predictive control. In contrast, this paper develops a control-centric framework for optimization itself, where algorithms are constructed directly from Lyapunov stability principles rather than being proposed first and analyzed afterward. A key element is the stationarity mapping, which encodes first-order optimality conditions and enables Lyapunov-based convergence analysis. By pairing a Lyapunov function with a selectable decay law, we obtain continuous-time dynamics with guaranteed exponential, finite-time, fixed-time, or prescribed-time convergence. The convergence regime thus becomes a design input: choosing among these regimes changes only the decay law, not the algorithm or its analysis. Within this framework, we introduce three feedback realizations of increasing restrictiveness: the Hessian-gradient, Newton, and gradient dynamics. These constructions unify unconstrained optimization, extend to constrained problems via Lyapunov-consistent primal-dual dynamics, and broaden results for minimax and generalized Nash equilibrium seeking problems beyond exponential stability, the last two through centralized solvers. In total, the framework spans six problem classes and four convergence regimes, yielding a unified design recipe across twenty-four combinations, some of which, to the best of our knowledge, have no direct continuous-time counterpart in the prior literature.
Systems and Control.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. 25 pages, 6 figures

Systems and Control.title: FedRIC: Heterogeneity-Aware Federated Learning with Hard Deadline Constraints in Open RAN
Systems and Control.summary: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RANs) bring intelligence to disaggregated RANs through virtualized platforms and open interfaces, but the stringent latency budgets of the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) and heterogeneous traffic conditions make real-time deployment costly. Centralized learning is ill-suited to the RIC due to its computational burden, timing constraints, and communication overhead, motivating Federated Learning (FL) as a distributed alternative. We formulate FL in O-RAN as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Program (MINLP) that minimizes communication cost and learning time under heterogeneity in User Equipment (UE) compute, traffic, and channel conditions, and decompose it into a UE Assignment (UA) subproblem and a Computation and Bandwidth Allocation (CBA) subproblem. We then propose FedRIC, a heterogeneity-aware FL framework combining compressed gradient descent, slice-aware resource allocation, and multilevel hierarchical aggregation. Experiments show that FedRIC outperforms FedCOM, FedAvg, and QFedAvg in convergence rate, communication cost, and latency.
Systems and Control.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Accepted for publication in the proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Interdisciplinary Applications (IEEE ISAIA), October 9-10, 2026. Montclair, US

Systems and Control.title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
Systems and Control.summary: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.

Systems and Control.title: Controller- and Communication-Aware Flexibility Margins for Electric Distribution Networks
Systems and Control.summary: This paper develops a framework for quantifying operational flexibility in radial electric distribution systems under coupled active- and reactive-load uncertainty. Flexibility is defined as the largest scaling of a prescribed uncertainty set that can be accommodated while satisfying network and actuator limits under a given control architecture. We consider a one-sided Euclidean set for robust demand-growth capability, with a direct extension to bidirectional variations. Under LinDistFlow, controllable distributed resources and feeder-head exchange with the upstream grid jointly balance active-power disturbances, while local Volt/VAR feedback regulates reactive power. The resulting affine closed-loop disturbance response admits exact second-order-cone robust counterparts. For fixed Volt/VAR gains, a convex reformulation jointly optimizes the flexibility margin and active-power participation factors, including feeder-head participation. A sparse load-to-generator feedforward map further captures communication constraints. Numerical studies on the Iowa-240 feeder demonstrate how the amount of control authority and communication structure shape the achievable flexibility margin.
Systems and Control.comment: 11 pages

Systems and Control.title: X-Safe: Embodiment-Agnostic Safeguarding for Robot Arm Manipulation Policies via Action Masking
Systems and Control.summary: Ensuring safety of learning-enabled robotic manipulation across diverse embodiments and tasks still requires significant manual engineering. For collision avoidance, existing approaches typically rely on embodiment-specific learned safety approximations or simplified robot models together with stopping-based fallback controllers that compromise performance. In this paper, we propose an embodiment-agnostic safeguarding approach, X-Safe, which provides formal probabilistic guarantees for collision avoidance without model simplifications or learned safety functions. By operating in the configuration space, our safeguarding method works with different types of robot policies. X-Safe reasons locally around the current configuration to establish safe regions and uses action masking to restrict the policy's support to these safe regions. We demonstrate X-Safe on two embodiments and three policies, both in simulation and on hardware. We observe less than half of the performance degradation compared to state-of-the-art safeguarding, and empirically corroborate our formal collision avoidance guarantees.

Systems and Control.title: A Practical Framework for Incremental Testing and Technology Maturation of Spacecraft Autonomy
Systems and Control.summary: This paper addresses the "trust gap" in deploying AI-enabled spacecraft autonomy through an integrated verification framework combining offline ground testing with online flight monitoring. The offline phase progresses systematically through simulation studies, processor-in-the-loop (PIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and robotic emulation testing, culminating in flight validation. The online phase employs AI watchdog systems for performance monitoring and safety guardrails for real-time constraint enforcement. Key contributions include: (1) systematic organization of verification techniques emphasizing closed-loop behavioral testing at each phase, (2) integration of AI watchdogs with runtime assurance, and (3) demonstration of the framework through a reinforcement learning-based attitude control case study. This approach integrates mature technologies to provide a viable pathway for safe deployment of AI-enabled autonomy in high-consequence space operations while addressing simulation-to-reality transfer challenges.

Systems and Control.title: VIGOR-MPC: Vision-Guided Objective Regulation MPC
Systems and Control.summary: Controlling an agent in an environment solely perceived through onboard vision is challenging: perception yields noisy, variable-length, and partially occluded context, while onboard compute is shared between perception and control, limiting the planning horizon executable in real time. We propose VIGOR-MPC, a modular student-teacher framework, agnostic to the perception pipeline, which addresses reference tracking across navigation tasks by distilling a privileged, field-of-view-aware long-horizon MPC into a computationally lightweight short-horizon MPC whose cost parameters are determined online from vision. The teacher operates in simulation with full state knowledge and a multi-trajectory formulation that guarantees the agent can stay within its field of view. The student observes only the noisy, occluded context produced by a perception module and learns, via a multi-level recurrent mapping, to infer cost parameters that aim to recover the teacher's behavior despite missing information. We evaluate VIGOR-MPC on vision-based autonomous racing in simulation and on hardware. Using only onboard perception of the track, VIGOR-MPC generalizes to tracks unseen during training and approaches the lap times of the privileged long-horizon teacher while reducing per-step computation by over 90%.

Systems and Control.title: Delay-Enabled Adaptive Learning of Time-Varying Parameters
Systems and Control.summary: This paper proposes a novel adaptive learning method for unknown time-varying parameters by deliberately incorporating a delay into the parameter update. Specifically, a conventional adaptive estimator is augmented with only one additional dynamic state, which estimates the parameter variation rate from the difference between current and previous parameter estimates. The method fundamentally changes the influence of time variation on estimation performance: the resulting estimation error is governed by the second derivative of the unknown parameter rather than its first derivative. Under persistent excitation, a small-gain analysis proves exponential stability of the complete estimation-error system and establishes explicit bounds for the parameter, state-prediction, and parameter-rate errors. In particular, accurate learning of linearly time-varying parameters and their unknown rates can be guaranteed with errors converging exponentially fast to zero. Numerical comparisons with conventional adaptive estimation and a recent timevarying parameter estimator demonstrate superior learning performance in the considered examples. The proposed delay-enabled adaptive estimator requires neither state derivatives nor any assumed model of parameter variation, and its implementation consists of one delayed difference and a first-order filter. These results thus provide a direct extension of adaptive learning from constant to time-varying parameters without sacrificing the simplicity of the conventional adaptive estimation mechanism.

Systems and Control.title: Asynchronous Distributed Multi-Sensor Fusion Over Sensor Track Hypotheses
Systems and Control.summary: This work proposes a multi-target tracking solution that reasons over combinations of sensor-level tracks to perform distributed multiple hypothesis tracking (MHT) in an asynchronous multi-sensor network. This approach handles clustered target tracking and allows for efficient information pedigree summarization for distributed data fusion (DDF). By decomposing the association problem into partitioned hypothesis sets and fusing across sensor track combinations, the method reduces combinatorial complexity compared to traditional MHT approaches. Evaluation on a satellite constellation-based tracking scenario demonstrates improved estimation accuracy and data association quality compared to a reference target tracker with global nearest neighbor association.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Multisensor Fusion and Integration (MFI), Plzeň. 6 pages, 6 figures

Systems and Control.title: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Robust Planetary Landing
Systems and Control.summary: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies for planetary landing and other aerospace guidance, navigation, and control tasks are commonly trained under randomized disturbances to improve robustness. However, typical stochastic perturbation sampling assumes independent variations, whereas real mission disturbances often exhibit spatial and temporal correlation and cannot be reproduced through independent random draws. This work investigates adversarial reinforcement learning to discover challenging off-nominal conditions. A secondary agent generates physically constrained perturbations that degrade the performance of a landing controller, forming an asymmetric sequential zero-sum game. Training proceeds in three stages: baseline controller learning, robustness enhancement with stochastic perturbations, and an iterative adversarial phase in which the controller and disturbance generator are alternately optimized. Preliminary experiments in a three-degree-of-freedom landing environment show that adversarial disturbances reveal vulnerabilities missed by conventional randomization and provide early indications that, with a more extensive training campaign, the approach can yield improved robustness and stronger generalization under previously unseen perturbation regimes.

Systems and Control.title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
Systems and Control.summary: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. The effectiveness and computational efficiency of the approach are demonstrated using experimentally obtained frequency response data from industrial-grade semiconductor equipment. The synthesized controller is implemented on the physical setup, and its performance is validated in real-time experiments.
authors: Maurice W. P. M. H. Heemels
Systems and Control.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, none other publications

Systems and Control.title: Enabling Tidying Tasks in Robotic Vacuum Cleaners via a Geometry-Induced Self-Locking Deployable Linkage
Systems and Control.summary: Robotic vacuum cleaners must extend their functionality within tight limits on size, cost, and durability. Deployable linkages with few actuators meet these limits, but their backdrivability makes it difficult to hold a load-bearing posture without continuous motor torque. We introduce a two-stage deployable linkage that is self-locking, in the sense used for toggle and singularity-based linkages, through its own geometry: at full deployment an internal three-link subchain approaches a collinear, near-singular configuration where the input--output transmission ratio approaches zero, so that plate loads produce a small residual back-driving torque, absorbed by drive-train friction and a lightweight magnetic detent. A single actuator performs deployment and locking, a passive chassis-mounted trigger releases the lock for retraction, and a second actuator adjusts only the deployment height. We integrate the mechanism into a commercial robotic vacuum cleaner and validate it through a 100-cycle repeatability test, a quasi-static load test in which the locked plate held 50\,N with the motor de-energized, and 140 pushing-type tidying trials on seven household objects against a commercial arm-equipped vacuum robot under a documented protocol. We derive the analytical holding condition and discuss its limits as an intermediate design point between passive compliance and articulated manipulation.
Systems and Control.comment: Research conducted in October 2025

Systems and Control.title: The Cost of Executability: Temporal Margins for Continuous-Time Multi-Agent Path Finding under Closed-Loop Control
Systems and Control.summary: Multi-agent path finding (MAPF) solvers are evaluated on the schedules they produce, not on how well those schedules can be executed. Specifically, continuous-time optimal solvers can achieve even lower cost than their discrete counterparts by scheduling agents with near-zero temporal/spatial separation, and by exploiting graphs with higher connectedness; however, such schedules may prove hard to execute under a realistic controller. We integrate AOC-CBS, an anytime-optimal continuous-time MAPF solver, into a fleet coordination framework in which each agent tracks its timed path using model predictive control, and we evaluate the resulting system on congested MovingAI benchmark instances with 21 to 40 agents. Without intervention, only a fraction of the instances complete execution. We then apply T-robustness by adding a time-margin, i.e., a minimum temporal gap between agents at shared locations, as well as spatial inflation of the agent footprint. Increasing either margin raises execution success, for a relatively small increase in the schedule's sum-of-costs; it also improves how closely agents adhere to the schedule: when tracking each agent's position throughout execution and comparing it against the position it should occupy according to the schedule, the mean discrepancy falls significantly as the margin increases. In general, the two margins have different effects; temporal margin decreases deviation, giving the controller room to stay on schedule. Spatial margin affects deviation less and instead increases the clearance between agents, so that the same deviation no longer leads to a blocking stall. They are nonetheless substitutes rather than complements: spatial inflation is almost free in schedule cost, but its effect on execution success is small and does not compound with a temporal margin already in place.

Systems and Control.title: Congestion-Aware Charging Coordination for Electric Ride-Hailing Fleets under Stochastic Demand
Systems and Control.summary: In this study, we develop a dynamic charging scheduling method that integrates day-ahead charging planning and online reactive vehicle dispatch and charger assignment. The day-ahead planning model minimizes expected charging costs by considering anticipated waiting times and overnight energy replenishment costs. The online model then adapts this plan by maximizing the profit from vehicle dispatching and assigning vehicles to chargers through a reservation-based charging request scheduler to minimize the total charging-related operational time. The developed charging policy is tested on a Manhattan-like study area using synthetic data drawn from NYC yellow taxi data with a fleet size of 100 vehicles given the scenarios of 3000 and 4000 customers/day. The computational results show that our method outperforms different benchmark policies with up to +21.68% profit and +22.22% service rate for 4000 customers relative to the weakest benchmark. Sensitivity analyses are conducted for different system parameters, and managerial insights are discussed.

Systems and Control.title: Radial-Angular Resolution Framework for Near-Field Communications
Systems and Control.summary: Near-field beamfocusing confines radiated power into a localized three-dimensional focal spot, making the analytical characterization of radial and angular resolution critical for sixth-generation (6G) multi-user systems, yet existing models treat the focal resolution as a fixed geometric outcome rather than a tunable design variable. Based on the Angular Representation (ASR) approach, this paper presents a resolution framework to design contiguous focal regions across both the radial and angular domain for steered multi-user systems. By extending the definition of a tunable inter-beam overlap $ρ$, we derive closed-form expressions for the radial and angular focal boundaries and extents, alongside the steering-dependent minimum focal distance $d_{0,\text{min}}$ and maximum steering angle $θ_{\text{max}}$. Using these boundaries, iterative synthesis algorithms are developed to construct uniform and non-uniform radial and angular beam arrangements. Finally, by analyzing both isolated and joint radial-angular configurations, we quantify the fundamental trade-offs between $ρ$, achievable user capacity, inter-user interference, and system sum-rate across varying steering angles.
Systems and Control.comment: 12 pages, 10 figures

Systems and Control.title: Sequential Learning-Based Physics-Informed Neural Network Modeling for Parameter Estimation on a Power Converter
Systems and Control.summary: A staged physics-informed neural network (PINN) is proposed for identifying the inductance, capacitance and parasitic resistances of a DC buck converter from time-domain data. Gradients are released in the order of L to C to rL to rC, a sequence derived from sensitivity analysis. The five-stage schedule recovers L and C to within 5% and the series ESR to 10%, while a three-stage variant attains the same accuracy 11% faster. An 84 factorial sweep confirms that the trained PINN remains accurate for simultaneous 8% perturbations of all four components, achieving a waveform RMSE of 2.6 x 10-2 over 5 ms-an order-of-magnitude better than a simultaneous-training baseline.
Systems and Control.comment: IEEE ECCE 2026

Systems and Control.title: Bang-Bang Evasion: Its Stochastic Optimality and a Terminal-Set-Based Implementation
Systems and Control.summary: We address the problem of optimal evasion in a planar endgame engagement, where a target with bounded lateral acceleration seeks to avoid interception by a missile guided by a linear feedback law. Contrary to existing approaches, that assume perfect information or use heuristic maneuver models in stochastic settings, we formulate the problem in an inherently stochastic framework involving imperfect information and bounded controls. Complying with the generalized separation theorem, the control law factors in the posterior distribution of the state. We extend the well-known optimality of bang-bang evasion maneuvers in deterministic settings to the realm of realistic, stochastic evasion scenarios. First, we prove that an optimal evasion strategy always exists, and that the set of optimal solutions includes at least one bang-bang policy, rendering the resulting optimal control problem finite-dimensional. Second, leveraging this structure, we propose the closed-loop terminal-set-based evasion (TSE) strategy, and demonstrate its effectiveness in simulation against a proportional navigation pursuer. Monte Carlo simulations show that the TSE strategy outperforms traditional stochastic evasion strategies based on random telegraph, Singer, and weaving models.
Systems and Control.comment: Published in the Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics. 31 pages, 4 figures

Systems and Control.title: Topology-adaptive Estimation of Maximum Voltage Unbalance for Distribution Networks with Finite-sample Guarantee
Systems and Control.summary: High penetration of single-phase distributed power production and frequent topology changes can significantly increase voltage unbalance in distribution networks. Reliable probabilistic power flow (PPF) assessment for the network, therefore, must account for topology-dependent power-flow equations, numerical error in the voltage unbalance factor (VUF), and finite-sample uncertainty in power measurements. In this paper, we propose Topology-Adaptive Certified Quantile Estimation (TACQE) to estimate the maximum VUF across monitored electric buses.
